name: application-device-toggle-tile
title: Device Toggle Tile
description: Smart-home device tile grid with a device icon, name, and an on/off toggle switch, with status text driven by real per-tile toggle state.
useWhen: Building a smart-home or IoT dashboard where users control multiple devices from one grid.
Each device benefits from a recognizable icon and immediate on/off status alongside the control.
You want the toggle's track color to reinforce the device's current state (green when on).
avoidWhen: You're toggling a plain user preference/setting, not a physical device — use `preference-toggle-row` instead, which fits list-style settings better.
The device has more than a binary on/off state (e.g. dimming, temperature) — extend this pattern with the appropriate control rather than forcing a toggle.
You need a dense list of many devices — a tile grid works best for a handful; consider a list layout at larger scale.
responsiveBehavior: Two-column grid by default; adjust grid-cols via className for wider dashboard layouts with more tiles per row.
accessibility: The toggle is a real checkbox input wrapped in its own <label>, so it is keyboard operable and has a correct accessible name from the visual label context.
On/off status is communicated by both the toggle position and visible status text ("On", "Off", "Locked"), not the track color alone.
Device name and status text dim together when a device is off, reducing visual weight without hiding the tile or its control.

variants.title: Device Toggle Tile
variants.description: Four device tiles: a light and thermostat on, a lock and plug off, each with an icon and toggle.
accessibility: Toggling a tile's switch updates real per-device state, changing the status text and track color together.

variants.title: Device Toggle Tile (Dark)
variants.description: Device toggle tile grid adapted for dark surfaces.
accessibility: Icon background/text and status colors are tuned to meet WCAG AA contrast against the dark surface.
